meta.paper: Hawk: An Efficient NALM System for Accurate Low-Power Appliance Recognition, SenSys '24
meta.note: Each claim's quote is an exact slice of ONE line of paper.txt: the PDF is two-column, and pdftotext -layout interleaves the right column into the same lines, so a quote that crossed a line break would splice in unrelated column text. Every number rendered on screen or spoken in src/hawk/script.ts should have a row here; note=null means the attribution is direct. Entries whose note starts with DERIVED, ILLUSTRATION, SYNTHETIC or UNSOURCED are the ones not backed by a literal paper figure (or not present in eval.json/gray.json/wave.json).

claims.quote: a widely used dataset, Hawk achieves an average F1 score of 93.94%
claims.note: AMBIGUITY: the abstract's one sentence covers two datasets - 'In HawkDATA and a widely used dataset ... 93.94% for state recognition and 97.07% for event recognition'. Section 1 (l.93-94) gives the exact split: 93.94 is state on HawkDATA (Section 1 prints 93.93; Figure 16 label and eval.json headline both 93.94), 97.07 is event on BLUED. On-screen value = eval.headline.stateAvgF1 (93.94, HawkDATA).

claims.quote: 92.71% for event recognition and 93.93% for state identification in
claims.note: Section 1 states event 92.71 / state 93.93 on HawkDATA; the abstract's '97.07% for event recognition' belongs to BLUED (Table 2), not HawkDATA. On-screen value = eval.headline.eventAvgF1 (92.71). Paper is internally inconsistent (93.93 vs 93.94); not corrected here.

claims.quote: improved state recognition accuracy by 47.98% to 48.07%
claims.note: Paper words it as a 47.98% accuracy increase over SOTA (and 48.07% on the next line); eval.json records stateGainPct 47.98 and the script renders 'percentage points'. Read as percentage points per eval.json; the paper's own unit is ambiguous.
Table 2 Average F1 for Hawk on BLUED. The abstract attributes 97.07% to event recognition in 'a widely used dataset' (= BLUED); HawkDATA event F1 is 92.71.
SOTA baseline column in Table 2 (average F1 85.50%); eval.json blued.mtsShapeletAvg = 85.5. The quote spans the whole Average row (dashes are its empty columns), so it also contains Hawk's 97.07.

claims.quote: outperforms MTS-Shapelet by 11.57%
claims.note: Paper says 'outperforms MTS-Shapelet by 11.57%', i.e. difference between 97.07 and 85.50 (eval.json deltaAvg 11.57); rendered as percentage points.

Table 4 Average column for the 5-appliance residential deployment. Note the paper is inconsistent: abstract says 96.02, Section 1 (l.96) says 96.03; on-screen uses Table 4's 96.02 (eval.field.residenceAvg).
Table 4 Average for the 6-appliance office deployment (5 of them low-power); consistent across abstract, Section 1 and Table 4.
